scenes.headline: One latent for a scene, a surface at any size
scenes.sub: How Surflo reconstructs 3D from a few photos
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tobiah. Let me show you Surflo. It turns a handful of ordinary photos into one clean 3D surface.

scenes.text: Geometry looks the same from every angle, so Surflo squeezes any number of views into one fixed latent and flows the surface points out of it.
scenes.label: The idea

scenes.title: Views in, one state, points out

steps.say: A frozen VGGT reads your unposed photos into patch tokens. A Perceiver pours them into 128 latent queries.
That is the whole scene, as one fixed-size global state, whatever the view count.
A flow decoder transports each query point, on its own, from noise onto the surface.

scenes.title: What flow matching does per point

parts.say: It should end on the surface.

parts.note: the decoder predicts the velocity along this line
parts.say: The decoder only predicts the velocity that walks one to the other.

scenes.label: numbers in the latent, for any scene
scenes.say: The latent is always 128 tokens wide, 65,536 numbers, whether two photos go in or eighty.

scenes.title: Guidance: making the points agree
scenes.say: Independent points can disagree, so guidance makes neighbours talk near the end of the flow.

items.say: First, guess where each point is heading.
Render them as little Gaussians, compare to the real photos, and nudge them to match.
Turn that correction into a velocity, and take the step.

scenes.text: A scene is one fixed-size state; the surface is as many points as you ask for.

scenes.say: Compress the views into one state, flow the points out, and let guidance make them agree.
